name: Autonomous Ferrofluid Denial Platform AFDP-2 'Tidemark'
description:
The AFDP-2 is a low-profile hovering drone platform roughly the size of a serving tray, carrying a pressurized reservoir of magnetically responsive ferrofluid suspension. It operates as a semi-autonomous area-denial system, releasing controlled ferrofluid streams across surfaces, doorways, and personnel at operator-designated coordinates. Once applied, an onboard induction coil array activates the fluid into a dynamic magnetic lattice, locking it in place or directing it toward ferromagnetic materials—including cybernetic implants, weapons, and armor reinforcement rods.

The Tidemark's defining characteristic is its dual-mode operation. In 'seal' mode, the platform coats surfaces with a hardening ferrofluid barrier that bonds magnetically to metallic structures, jamming doors, immobilizing vehicles, and fouling mechanical joints. In 'hunt' mode, the platform releases a free-flowing suspension that tracks ferromagnetic signatures and migrates toward them, infiltrating ventilation gaps, armor seams, and cybernetic port covers before the induction coil locks it rigid—immobilizing limbs, jamming weapon actions, and in high-concentration applications, compressing cybernetic housings enough to cause internal hardware failure.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the AFDP-2 for military perimeter denial and hostage containment scenarios, but the platform's 'hunt' mode quickly attracted the attention of extraction specialists and intelligence operatives who recognized its value for non-lethal asset capture. The fluid reservoir is field-replaceable, and a thriving black market exists for modified suspension compounds with enhanced conductivity or caustic additives.
specifications: platform dimensions: 480mm x 320mm x 90mm platform weight: 3.8 kg (empty reservoir) fluid reservoir capacity: 2.2 liters standard suspension operational modes: Seal mode, Hunt mode, Purge mode (rapid full dispersal) hover endurance: 22 minutes on internal cell effective range: Up to 40 meters from operator induction coil output: 0.8 Tesla localized field ferrofluid bond strength: Sufficient to immobilize standard servo-assisted limbs reservoir swap time: ~15 seconds with field kit
tactical_use: Military operators use the AFDP-2 to seal building entry points ahead of a breach—coating door frames, vent covers, and stairwell rails with hardened ferrofluid to channel opposition movement. In close-quarters operations, 'hunt' mode is released into a room before entry, allowing the suspension to migrate toward armed targets and foul their weapon mechanisms before the team moves in. Intelligence operatives use low-volume 'hunt' releases to selectively immobilize a single target's cybernetic arm while leaving them otherwise mobile—enabling capture without confrontation. Operators always carry a magnetic purge wand to de-activate fluid applied to allied equipment.
cultural_context: The AFDP-2 occupies an unusual cultural space in GLMZ: it is simultaneously a symbol of state-level military capability and, increasingly, a trophy weapon among elite criminal organizations who see its acquisition as proof of their reach into military supply chains. Its non-lethal primary function makes it philosophically interesting to certain factions—the Tidemark is a weapon of control, not destruction, and organizations that prize asset capture over elimination actively seek it out. Street-level rumors about 'the black water' that freezes your chrome in place have given the weapon an almost mythological reputation in augmented communities.
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS covert operations divisions
High-tier criminal organizations with military supply access
Corporate espionage operatives specializing in asset recovery
story_hooks: A shipment of AFDP-2 units has gone missing from a military logistics depot—someone inside ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS is feeding equipment to a third party, and the players are hired to trace the leak.

A target the players need to extract has been sealed inside a building by a Tidemark in seal mode—the doors are magnetically bonded shut and the platform is still active inside, running low on power but unpredictable.

A black-market chemist is selling a modified ferrofluid compound that, once activated, cannot be de-activated by standard purge wands—someone wants this formula suppressed before it reaches the open market.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flat, angular hovering platform resembling a tactical serving tray with aggressive geometric edges. Low center of gravity, four corner-mounted thruster pods visible as raised cylindrical housings. The dominant visual feature is a translucent central reservoir tank occupying 60% of the upper surface, revealing swirling ferrofluid in constant slow motion—dark metallic suspension that catches light with an oily, magnetic shimmer. The platform reads as purposefully minimalist: military-grade, no wasted geometry.
physical_description.dimensions: 480mm length × 320mm width × 90mm height (platform body); reservoir protrusion adds ~25mm; thruster pods extend another 40mm downward
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and compact—feels deliberately engineered for stability despite ferrofluid's viscous load. The 3.8 kg dry platform suggests heft in hand, but the hovering operational state renders weight irrelevant; visually it conveys controlled heaviness, not bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-alloy chassis frame with reinforced polymer mounting brackets. Reservoir constructed from specialized ferrofluidity-compatible acrylic or polycarbonate composite to contain the suspension without degradation.
physical_description.finish: Matte anthracite-gray anodized titanium with brushed micro-texture to reduce reflectivity. Reservoir housing features a slight satin finish to minimize glare while remaining transparent. All edges beveled and sharp—industrial military aesthetic.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-gray chassis as primary; deep metallic black ferrofluid suspension (appears as dark iron-oxide slurry); accent lighting in cold blue LED indicators along thruster pods and a thin red status line running the platform's perimeter when active
physical_description.grip_texture: Not designed for handheld operation—platform features four discrete magnetic clamp points on underside for secure transport or docking. Top surface has minimal texture—smooth acrylic reservoir and recessed control nodes featuring rubberized tactile buttons for field-mode selection.
distinctive_features: Translucent ferrofluid reservoir dominating upper surface with visible swirling magnetic particulates
Four cylindrical thruster pods positioned at corners, each topped with intake vents and exhaust nozzles
Recessed induction coil array visible as faint circular copper traces beneath polymer floor panel
Red magnetic activation indicator line that glows during 'hunt' mode operation
Magnetic field visualization grid etched into top surface—technical reference markings
Quick-release titanium latch system for reservoir swap (two corner-mounted lever locks)
Faint wear marks and scratched areas on lower thruster pods suggesting field deployment history
Pneumatic pressure gauge (small analog dial) mounted on starboard edge of reservoir
Three discrete indicator LEDs: blue (power), amber (reservoir low), red (induction active)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (geometric triangular design) stamped in raised relief on port edge of frame—unpainted bare titanium. Serial designation 'AFDP-2 TIDEMARK' etched below manufacturer mark in clean sans-serif font. Military contract number stenciled on starboard thruster pod in white phosphorescent paint. No commercial branding—purely functional military identification.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Thruster pods show scuff marks and minor micro-fractures from environmental exposure. Reservoir remains pristine (regularly swapped), but the frame exhibits fine scratches from equipment handling and deployment in harsh terrain. Some ferrofluid residue may appear dried on lower edges—sign of active operational use. Overall condition: battle-ready, no visible corrosion, all systems functional.
